title: Which engine to choose for AI Claude code and codex?
author: Particular_Nose7732
selftext:
Unreal engine vs unity vs godot For complete Ai workflow

 I am a full stack dev,  I have no experience in game dev.

I am leaning towards Unreal engine but fear is not the best for AI.

  
my second Option is godot.

based on your experience which is the best for ai, for 3d horror game.

comments.author: madebymoss
comments.body:
I usually just let it pick the best one based on the request, because different scenarios may need different engines. TBH I feel AI knows this better than me.

With the help of AI is also possible to make change at a later stage. So I would say it's an important decision, but don't let it block you from moving on and start building :)

comments.author: FragmentedHeap
comments.body:
You could be crazy like me, and build one from scratch using claude in rust/csharp with .net 11 AOT and runtime async support.

I'm building everything from scratch on rust wgpu native, rust winit, and on and on.  Even built mtsdf text rendering engine from scatch, also sound studio/library, and it's all cross platform out of the box.

Any game I make with it will run on linux/mac/windows out of the box.

Still working on it.

If I were going to pick one though, I'd probably go with Godot or Monogame, but Monogame is anti AI and it has a lot of issues and they don't accept AI pr's, so Godot.

comments.author: FreeQ1337
comments.body: I'm using godot and it works really well. Especially that most of it is plain text so Claude works well with it.

comments.author: Dreamt_Up_Games
comments.body: I’m using Unity because that is what I was already familiar with and it works great with the Unity CLI.

comments.author: 5ingle5hot
comments.body: I doubt any of the popular engines will be better/worse with AI compared to each other. I chose Godot for my first game about 17 months ago and used AI to author code, and now have around 140k lines of GDScript and am a few months away from a Steam release. No vibe coding. Software engineering with AI. I used to use the Godot editor but it's been months since I've opened it. One thing I did that was a big help was build an MCP server in my game in development mode allowing my agent to dig into the game while it's running. I can say "hey I expect X but its Y, check it out" and it will poke around, take screenshots and analyze them, etc. - it really helps with debugging and tweaking. Anyway... this is just an anecdote that I am probably similar to you, and I really like Godot. I'm all-in on AI as a development tool.

comments.author: Jason9mm
comments.body: I made one game with Claude and Godot, with no coding experience, and I think it went great. I really can't think what I'd want to add in there. I just type what a want into the terminal and code goes straight to Godot. It's pretty freaking handy.

comments.author: Hotwingz66
comments.body:
Godot and codex work very smoothly.

Can recommend it.
But do read up on Godot pros and cons.
